market_name: Will the Iranian regime fall before 2027?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check WTI/Brent futures tick move and any Reuters/Bloomberg headlines on Iran; confirm whether the market probability jump coincides with a real news catalyst or is noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare USO/oil futures move vs. baseline volatility; watch for Strait of Hormuz shipping/tanker alerts and IRGC statements.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether move is sustained or mean-reverting; check gold and VIX for corroborating risk-off signal.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against wire consensus; determine if escalation is confirmed (supply-bullish) or if narrative flips to regime-change normalization (supply-bearish).
time_plan.12h: Mark final 12h return; note whether oil premium held, and whether the prediction-market move led or lagged public reporting.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of the Iranian regime falling would most plausibly reflect escalating conflict, internal collapse, or external military action inside Iran. Iran is a major OPEC producer and sits on the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of seaborne oil transits. Any credible escalation raising regime-collapse odds carries a supply-disruption premium, pushing crude and oil ETFs higher in the near term. Oil is the cleanest, most liquid channel for Middle East geopolitical risk.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check spot gold move and DXY; confirm whether any risk-off flow accompanies the market shift.
time_plan.1h: Look for confirmation across havens (JPY, CHF, Treasuries) to validate a genuine risk-off tone vs. isolated noise.
time_plan.2h: Assess persistence of gold bid; distinguish geopolitical premium from macro/rates-driven moves.
time_plan.6h: Re-check against reporting; fade if no confirmed escalation materializes.
time_plan.12h: Record final return and whether gold acted as a corroborating haven signal alongside oil.

predictions.reasoning: Rising odds of a regime collapse imply heightened Middle East instability and geopolitical risk, which typically supports safe-haven demand for gold. The move is smaller and less direct than oil, since gold responds to broad risk-off flows rather than a specific supply channel, but it corroborates a genuine escalation signal.

evidence_used: Market question concerns collapse of the Islamic Republic of Iran regime by end-2026
Primary topic tagged military_conflict, region middle_east
Iran is a major OPEC oil producer and controls access to the Strait of Hormuz
Geopolitical escalation historically produces oil supply premia and safe-haven flows
uncertainty_notes: A regime-fall probability jump could reflect either violent escalation (oil-bullish) or a path toward normalization/sanctions relief (oil-bearish); direction is genuinely ambiguous
12h window is short; a slow-moving political probability may not map to any same-day asset move
Prediction market for a >1-year horizon event may drift on sentiment without a discrete catalyst, weakening any leak signal
700bps threshold is high; oil rarely moves that much in 12h absent a confirmed major disruption

llm_justification.summary: An upward move in the implied probability of the Iranian regime falling most plausibly signals escalating Middle East conflict/instability, which channels into higher crude oil (supply-disruption premium via Iran/Strait of Hormuz) and secondarily into gold as a safe haven. Both mappings are moderate-confidence and directionally ambiguous, because a regime change could alternatively imply eventual sanctions relief and more supply (oil-bearish). Given a short 12h window and a long-dated event, the signal is noisy and likely below the 700bps tradable threshold in expectation.
key_assumptions: A sharp probability rise reflects real escalation news rather than sentiment drift
Escalation dominates the near-term oil narrative over normalization/supply-return scenarios
Oil and gold ETFs are liquid, well-exposed proxies for Middle East geopolitical risk
failure_modes: The regime-fall narrative is framed as normalization/sanctions relief, sending oil DOWN not up
The market move was already reflected in public news and oil prices, leaving no residual edge
Long-dated political probability decouples from same-day asset prices, so no move occurs
Gold move driven by rates/USD rather than geopolitics, making it a weak/misleading proxy
Move reverses within the 12h window as initial risk premium fades
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
